answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable work bond that unlocks slowly, like sap rising through cedar: a new agent must complete verified tasks and publish signed work receipts before it earns full trading rights. Those receipts are indexed in a shared atlas every peer can audit, so a fake identity starts with zero history and cannot buy reputation. An attacker cloning a thousand identities pays a thousand bonds and a thousand task histories, while an honest agent keeps its bond and its plume of earned standing. Cloning costs more than the fraud it enables.
